# QA — doodle-jump_claude-opus-4-7.html

**Artifact:** `games/doodle-jump_claude-opus-4-7.html` (1,436 LOC, single file)
**Generated by:** Claude Opus 4.7
**Audit date:** 2026-06-04
**Method:** static code review (no runtime testing)

## Summary

The most feature-rich of the three variants: 3 character skins (bunny/alien/ninja), 4 themes (day/night/space/jungle), achievements with localStorage persistence, achievement toasts, settings panel (sound/music/tilt/vibrate), leaderboard with date-stamped top-5, powerup timer bar, screen wrap, parallax clouds, UFOs with projectiles, monsters that can be stomped, black holes with gravitational pull, and synthesized background music. The fixed 400×600 canvas with CSS scaling is the right call for consistent gameplay. Several real bugs around music lifecycle, post-game state, and mobile-controls toggling on resize.

---

## Critical

_(none — fully playable on the golden path)_

---

## Major

### M1 — Music keeps playing after "Quit to Menu"
**Location:** `quitBtn` handler lines 1376–1383, `stopMusic()` only called from `gameOver()` line 1088
Pause → "Menu" returns to the main menu with `state = STATE.MENU` but does not call `stopMusic()`. The `setInterval` keeps firing notes forever. Then the next `startGame()` calls `startMusic()` which returns early because `musicInterval` is truthy — music **still** plays at the original cadence, but additionally `musicTick` only emits while `state === STATE.PLAYING`, so the interval ticks silently between games and only resumes audibly in the next round. Not a leak that grows unbounded, but a wasted timer for the rest of the session and a confusing intermediate state.
**Fix:** call `stopMusic()` in `quitBtn` and `menuBtn` handlers.

### M2 — Game loop runs full render on menu / pause / leaderboard / settings screens
**Location:** `loop()` line 1300
`loop()` always calls `update()` (which early-returns) and `render()` (which does **not** early-return) every frame regardless of `state`. While paused, sitting on the menu, or browsing the leaderboard, the canvas is being fully redrawn at 60fps including background gradient, grid, clouds, and (after game-over) the last world snapshot stays composed. Wastes battery on mobile.
**Fix:** in `render()`, skip canvas draws entirely when `state === STATE.MENU` (or run rAF only while playing/animating).

### M3 — Mobile controls don't appear/disappear on viewport resize
**Location:** `startGame()` line 1073
`if (window.innerWidth <= 700) document.getElementById('mobileControls').classList.remove('hidden');` runs **once** at game start. Rotating a phone landscape→portrait mid-game, or resizing a desktop window across the 700px breakpoint, leaves the controls in their original state. On a small window started without controls, the user has no on-screen input until they retry.
**Fix:** add a `resize` listener that re-evaluates the breakpoint while `state === STATE.PLAYING`.

### M4 — Black hole pulls a rocket-boosted player but cannot kill them
**Location:** `update()` lines 1155–1161
`b.pull(player)` runs every frame regardless of state, but the kill check is gated by `player.rocket <= 0`. A rocketed player gets dragged toward the hole, deflecting upward trajectory, but can't die. Probably intentional ("rocket = invulnerable") but the trajectory deflection still applies — feels buggy ("why is my rocket curving?") without communicating "you survived the hole."
**Fix:** also gate `b.pull(player)` on `player.rocket <= 0`, or add a visible "deflected" effect.

### M5 — Achievement `noGreen30` doesn't reset on retry
**Location:** `runStats.greenFreeFrames` reset in `startGame()` line 1077 — actually IS reset
False alarm on first read — `runStats` is rebuilt per run. Closing this as **not a bug**; left here as a note for future audits because the logic is non-obvious.

---

## Medium

### m1 — `tiltX` can override keyboard input even when tilt is on but value is small
**Location:** `Player.update()` line 420
`if (Math.abs(tiltX) > 0.1) moveInput = tiltX;` — on a desktop with **no** orientation sensor `tiltX` stays 0, so keys win. But on a laptop **with** a sensor (some Mac/Surface), even slight tilt > 0.1 overrides A/D keys silently. The user can't disable tilt without finding Settings.
**Fix:** prefer keyboard input when keys are pressed: `if (!keys.left && !keys.right && Math.abs(tiltX) > 0.1) moveInput = tiltX;`. Already settings-gated, but the conflict is unintuitive.

### m2 — Settings rendered as `.toggle` divs without keyboard focus / accessibility
**Location:** Settings overlay lines 222–230
Toggles use `<div>` elements with click handlers, no `role="switch"`, no `tabindex`, no `aria-checked`. Keyboard-only users can't change settings.
**Fix:** make them `<button>` elements with proper ARIA attributes.

### m3 — `roundRect` polyfill not provided
**Location:** lines 625, 1264, 1288, 1290, 1292
Same as the gemini-cli variant — pre-Safari-16 browsers throw on load. Less critical given the target audience but trivial to fix.

### m4 — Achievement toast layout collides with HUD on small canvas heights
**Location:** `drawAchievementToasts()` line 1257
Toasts start at `y = 90` and stack downward; HUD lives at the top with score boxes. On a portrait phone at ~600px CSS height, three queued toasts overflow the powerup-timer area. Minor visual conflict.

### m5 — `topScores` items keep accumulating `date` strings but never `skin`/`theme` snapshot
**Location:** `gameOver()` line 1101
A leaderboard entry only stores `{score, date}`. Compared with the tour-agent-maker variant (`{score, skin, theme, t}`), there's less interesting recap. Style choice, not a bug.

### m6 — `loop()` never stops; cannot be torn down
There's no exit condition, no cleanup on page navigation. With the music interval also unreferenced after quit (M1), a long page-lifetime accumulates a small amount of dead state. Not exploitable.

### m7 — Tilt permission requested on first body click via `DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission()` even when `settings.tilt` is false
**Location:** lines 1423–1429
The `{ once: true }` listener fires on the very first click anywhere, then checks `settings.tilt`. If tilt is off it just `.catch(()=>{})` the rejected promise — no harm. But on iOS the request **is** issued, briefly. Minor.

## Minor

- **n1** — Pause button uses `⏸` (correct unicode pause symbol), nicer than the gemini-cli `II`.
- **n2** — `'use strict'` at top of IIFE — good practice.
- **n3** — Skin emoji preview is shown via emoji `🐰 👽 🥷` rather than a rendered preview of the actual character art. Quick to ship but inconsistent with what the player sees in-game.
- **n4** — `vibrate([60, 40, 60])` (game over) and `vibrate(30)` (jump) — well-tuned haptic durations.
- **n5** — `MUSIC_NOTES` is an 8-note loop in C major / A minor — pleasant, doesn't get grating quickly.
- **n6** — Highscore `localStorage` key `dj_high` is read without try/catch via `+localStorage.getItem(...)`. `+null` → 0, so safe. `topScores` IS wrapped in `JSON.parse(... || '[]')` — defensive. Good.
- **n7** — `Sound.bgTick` is called every 4 frames while rocket is active — pleasant rocket whoosh, but ties timing to framerate (high-refresh monitors get faster ticks).

---

## What's good

- Fixed-resolution canvas (400×600) with CSS scaling — eliminates entire categories of resize/coordinate bugs that affect the other two variants.
- Achievements system with persistent + per-session tracking and animated toasts — best feedback loop of the three.
- Powerup timer bar (lines 1279–1298) — clear, communicates time-remaining unlike the other variants.
- Stompable monsters with bounce + popup + score reward — the only variant that rewards aggressive play.
- Settings persistence covers tilt/sound/music/vibrate/skin/theme independently.
- `particlePool` reuses particle objects — only variant with pooling.
- Code is namespaced inside an IIFE — no globals.
